messages:
Alex: Morning chaos  power flicker here, desk lamp and router rebooted. Had to join standup on phone tether. Anyone got creative hotspot names? I used "tiny-signal-big-ideas" :phone:

Priya: hah nice. Check if your ISP sent an outage alert? sometimes it's local transformer stuff.

Jin: If it's brief, tethering is fine. For longer outages, a cheap LTE hotspot or old phone on a prepaid plan is handy.

Alex: Ran a quick ping during the flicker and saw wild spikes, pasted below:

Alex: ```
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 bytes of data.
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=18.4 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=117 time=512.7 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=117 time=19.1 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 3 received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 18.4/183.4/512.7 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed alex-laptop transient spike at 2390012402, peak RTT 513ms, event count 5 in last 30m. Suggested: tether or schedule meeting handoff if outage persists.

Carla: Quick poll  react with :battery: for "buy a UPS for the router", :phone: for "use phone tether", :coffee: for "move to a cafe".

Priya: UPS is worth it if blips are frequent. For rare outages, tether + cafe is cheaper and more fun.

Alex: Ordered a small UPS and a $20 SIM-only backup. Will post the hotspot name and a survival selfie. :grin:

Carla: Pro-tip: disable auto-switch in your video app so calls don't glitch when you swap networks mid-meeting.

Alex: Thanks all  felt very supported. New hotspot name will be announced with ceremony.

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: alex-laptop events cleared at 2390012608; monitoring resumed.
